name: The Capital Suite
label: Old Colony Recordings
lede: Four Skidmore students from three class years made one album, Bekampa Tramset, at a studio down an Amherst dirt road. Twenty-four years later a Cape Cod label put it back out.

hero.by: WSPN's indie-rock night at Falstaff's, Skidmore College, March 14, 1997 · Photo: George Wilson

eras.title: A Rail guitarist on the campus radio
eras.text: Jamie Kennard came to Skidmore College from Fairport, outside Rochester, and played guitar in the Rochester emo-punk band Rail. Jon Hills, his classmate in the class of '97, spent 1994 to 1996 in Creepy Woods. Discogs dates the Capital Suite to 1996.

years.src: Skidmore News, Sep 15, 1994 · Skidmore News, Feb 24, 1994 · Skidmore News, May 21, 1996
years.h: Kennard and Chris Ott share a WSPN schedule
years.p: The Skidmore News prints the campus station's fall line-up, and both Jamie Kennard and Chris Ott have shows. Three years later Ott co-produced the Capital Suite's only album.
years.xp:
Kennard had been on WSPN since at least February 1994, on a punk show called Late Night Baby with Alexa Ciganer and Maura Hallowell.

A joke prediction in the paper in May 1996 had him further along: "Jamie Kennard is head of Dischord records."

years.src: Discogs: The Capital Suite · Discogs: Dan Crowell · Wikipedia: Black Army Jacket · Skidmore News, Apr 16, 1999
years.h: Discogs puts the Capital Suite's start at Skidmore in 1996
years.p: The line-up on the record: Jon Hills and Jamie Kennard on guitars and vocals, Terry Chatkupt on bass and vocals, Dan Crowell on drums.
years.xp:
Crowell, a first-year in the class of 2000, was already a hardcore drummer. He had played in Half Man, part of New York State's Mountain C.I.A. crew, and in the New York grindcore band Black Army Jacket, which Wikipedia says recruited him while he was still in high school.

Chatkupt, class of '99, was a studio art major from Kansas City.

eras.title: Ice storm in March, Amherst in December
eras.text: The one show on record is a WSPN night at Falstaff's, the campus club, where the headliners never made it. Hills and Kennard graduated that spring, and in December the band recorded in Amherst, Massachusetts, with Mark Alan Miller and Chris Ott.

years.h: Kennard books Falstaff's and lends bands his cellar
years.p: A Skidmore News feature on campus bands names Jamie Kennard '97, Rail's guitarist, as a student who books bands at Falstaff's. He also opens his off-campus cellar to on-campus musicians looking for a place to practice.
years.xp: His complaint to the paper: "I think that the issue with the practice space stunts the growth of a lot of bands." With better rooms, he said, "we'd have a lot more campus bands."

years.cap: A four-piece on stage at WSPN's indie night at Falstaff's, Skidmore College, March 14, 1997; the paper doesn't name the band in the photo · Photo: George Wilson
years.h: Karate cancels in an ice storm, and the Capital Suite plays anyway
years.p: WSPN had booked the Godrays and [[Karate|7d942b74-f556-49c5-8987-067dc0488c90]] for Falstaff's, and the weather kept both away. The Skidmore News says 7th Level Fighters and Regular Light "stepped in to help Capital Suite put on a great show."
years.xp: John Rodzvilla's report ran on March 20 under the headline "Neither rain nor sleet... WSPN's night of Indie Rock." It is the only time the band's name turns up in the Skidmore News archive.

years.src: Skidmore News, May 15, 1997 · Skidmore News, Feb 6, 1997
years.h: The Skidmore News senior issue makes predictions for Kennard and Hills
years.p: The Skidmore News senior issue: "Jamie Kennard- will be singing the sound of your future." And "Jon Hills- Thanking god every day for choosing art over geology."
years.xp: Hills graduated a studio art major. In February the paper's A&E Artist of the Week profile had him arguing that the computer is as much an artist's tool as a paintbrush.

years.src: Discogs: The Capital Suite, Bekampa Tramset · Valley Advocate: Mark Alan Miller
yt: Just the Ticket, Please, from Bekampa Tramset
years.h: Chris Ott co-produces the album at the Slaughterhouse in Amherst
years.p: The liner notes credit Miller as producer, "with Chris Ott (aka The Grace Period)" and the band, December 1997. Ott's own project is [[The Grace Period|c71fe634-2eab-4e3d-8b1c-473374b64301]].
years.xp: The Valley Advocate described the Slaughterhouse as "a small stark structure all by its lonesome down an Amherst dirt road." Miller later owned it, moved it to Westhampton, and in 2012 opened Sonelab in Easthampton.

eras.title: Catalog number one
eras.text: Kennard and Jim Hemingway mastered the tapes in February, and Kennard laid out the CD. It came out on Old Colony Recordings, a label with a PO box in Duxbury, Massachusetts, as its first release.

years.src: Discogs: The Capital Suite, Bekampa Tramset · Discogs: The Grace Period, Bekampa Tramset · Old Colony Recordings (archived site)
years.h: Old Colony Recordings opens with Bekampa Tramset
years.p: Nine songs on CD, from Just The Ticket, Please to the seven-minute closer Wire Tap, catalog COL001. Old Colony's second release, three years later, was Hills' [[1 Mile North|b0d6108a-3dd5-479d-b518-803f54b3ba45]].
years.xp:
Ott's Grace Period put out a CD the same year on Audio Dregs, also called Bekampa Tramset. Neither Discogs listing explains the shared title.

Old Colony's website, as archived in 2002, listed three bands: 1 Mile North, the Capital Suite and Kennard's Rail.

eras.title: The record comes back from 1997
eras.text: Crowell kept drumming, Chatkupt became a Los Angeles artist, and Hills kept 1 Mile North going. In 2022 Mutual Skies, the Cape Cod label that Discogs says Old Colony now trades as, brought the record back.

years.h: Crowell becomes Matt Pond PA's drummer
years.p: After co-founding Celebrity Murders in 2003, Dan Crowell joins Matt Pond PA, per Discogs, and plays on its records through 2020. Later he drums in Brooklyn's Violent Bullshit.

years.src: Skidmore News, Apr 16, 1999 · Skidmore Scope, Winter 2002 · Skidmore Scope, Fall 2003 · Terry Chatkupt: About · Irvine Valley College: Digital Media Art
years.h: Terry Chatkupt finishes an MFA at CalArts
years.p: After a year and a half at a New York gallery and a 2003 Skowhegan residency, Chatkupt becomes an LA artist and filmmaker who records as Terrain and plays in the duo Psychoplasmics.
years.xp: The Skidmore News profiled him in April 1999, a senior studio art major from Kansas City whose parents are from Thailand, planning to move to New York. The college's alumni magazine followed him to CalArts and Skowhegan. He now teaches digital media art at Irvine Valley College.

years.h: "It rips!" Crowell says of the record, 14 years on
years.p: Wishing Chatkupt a happy birthday on Facebook, Dan Crowell mentions he recently listened to the Capital Suite record.

years.src: Mutual Skies: The Capital Suite, Bekampa Tramset · Facebook: Dan Crowell, Sep 19, 2022 · Last.fm: The Capital Suite · Waterslide Records: Bekampa Tramset
years.p: The Cape Cod label puts the album on streaming and CD. Dan Crowell's Facebook post on September 19 adds: "Resurrected from 1997!"
years.xp:
Mutual Skies' tagline: "Upstate NY post-hardcore supergroup featuring members of Rail, 1 Mile North, Half Man and Black Army Jacket."

Before the reissue, a 2006 Last.fm note heard "slightly mathy and grooving emo / indie, similar to engine down and boys life," and a Japanese distro filed it next to June of 44 and Giant's Chair.
